body:
This issue is mostly focusing on organising MFA-related requirements. The key aspects for content should be agreed in #2970.

We have 2 MFA-related requirements in section "V6.3 General Authentication Security" but we also have a dedicated MFA-related section "V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements"

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **6.3.3** | Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. Relaxing this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls. | 2 | v5.0.be-2.2.9 |
| **6.3.8** | Verify that a hardware-based authentication mechanism is supported that provides impersonation resistance against phishing attacks (such as WebAuthn) and verifies intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key). | 3 | v5.0.be-2.2.4 |

Problem to solve 1 (must have): 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 are in conflict from the "accepted for L3" point of view (6.3.3 is accepted for L2 and L3, and 6.3.8 is accepted for L3). So I think we should merge it into one requirement with an in-requirement level description.

Problem to solve 2 (nice to have): We have a dedicated section for MFA, and it would be more logical to search MFA-related requirements from that section.

Additional (nice to have) topic: I would prioritize less password-related requirements and move them down in chapter order.

comments.body:
> Problem to solve 1 (must have): 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 are in conflict from the "accepted for L3" point of view (6.3.3 is accepted for L2 and L3, and 6.3.8 is accepted for L3). So I think we should merge it into one requirement with an in-requirement level description.

Why is this currently a problem. Are you preempting a situation where L3 changes to "required" rather than "supported"?

> Problem to solve 2 (nice to have): We have a dedicated section for MFA, and it would be more logical to search MFA-related requirements from that section.

Agree that makes sense.

> Additional (nice to have) topic: I would prioritize less password-related requirements and move them down in chapter order.

Not sure I would bother, these concerns are still relevant, especially at L1.

> > Problem to solve 1 (must have): 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 are in conflict from the "accepted for L3" point of view (6.3.3 is accepted for L2 and L3, and 6.3.8 is accepted for L3). So I think we should merge it into one requirement with an in-requirement level description.
> 
> Why is this currently a problem. Are you preempting a situation where L3 changes to "required" rather than "supported"?

6.3.8 is going to require hardware-based authentication, whereas 6.3.3 does not require it. Both are matching requirements for L3 - so one can say that "the application is aligned with ASVS L3 because of satisfying the requirement 6.3.3".

Basically we need to revert the split from v4.0.3-2.2.4: https://asvs.dev/mapping_v4.0.3_to_v5.0.0.html#v4.0.3-2.2.4

> Problem to solve 2 (nice to have): We have a dedicated section for MFA, and it would be more logical to search MFA-related requirements from that section.

Given that AAL3 becomes required for ASVS L3, when reorganizing, passkeys can be used as both single- and multi-factor or a combination of the two. It can quickly become confusing for the reader. I support this, but keep this in mind.

> Problem to solve 1 (must have): 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 are in conflict from the "accepted for L3" point of view (6.3.3 is accepted for L2 and L3, and 6.3.8 is accepted for L3). So I think we should merge it into one requirement with an in-requirement level description.

Not sure 6.3.3 need to become in conflict 6.3.8. 6.3.8 can be seen as including 6.3.3. This is because a single authentication session using device-bound passkeys must be configured to align with AAL3. eIDAS LoA3 authenticators are always multi-factor: https://www.lissi.id/sca

> Not sure 6.3.3 need to become in conflict 6.3.8

It already is in conflict - 6.3.3 accepting AAL2 at ASVS L3.
Doesn't AAL3 build on top of AAL2? https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3-Implementation-Resources/63B/AAL/
I am not sure it is necessary to map AAL2 to ASVS Level 2. AAL2's emphasis on physical authenticators seems archaic to me.

I only talk about requirements in ASVS and about the risk, that those may be interpreted the way we don't want. E.g. 6.3.3 is accepting NIST AAL2 at ASVS level 3. But seems that I'm not able to communicate the problem here.

We should have one requirement per one problem - at L3, at the moment we have 2 (6.3.3 and 6.3.8) - and they are asking different things for the same problem.

Just in case an example of the concept "in-requirement levels" based on 10.4.3:
> Verify that the authorization code is short-lived. The maximum lifetime can be up to 10 minutes for L1 and L2 applications and up to 1 minute for L3 applications.

> I only talk about requirements in ASVS and about the risk, that those may be interpreted the way we don't want. E.g. 6.3.3 is accepting NIST AAL2 at ASVS level 3. But seems that I'm not able to communicate the problem here.

I am not able to follow you. I would rather say that AAL3, IAL3, FAL3 and eIDAS LoA3 should be appropriate for satisfying 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2023/12/22/EU-US%20TTC%20WG1_Digital_Identity_Mapping_Report_Final%20Draft%20for%20Comment_22122023.pdf 

From the way I have formulated myself in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/3093/files, it should at least be possible to understand that if not completely clear. 

I would be careful about setting two equal signs between ASVS and AAL.
I just tried to explain "problem to solve 1" in a different way. If we leave all NIST away from the problem statement, the problem is still there. If it was not understandable so far, let it be.

Perhaps on the side, but AAL2 is in conflicts with itself.

> AAL2 requires the use of two authentication factors, either (1) a physical authenticator and a memorized secret, or (2) a physical authenticator and a biometric

https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3-Implementation-Resources/63B/AAL/

and

> Syncable authenticators may be offered as a new option for applications that seek to implement up to AAL2.

https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/syncable/

How does that even make sense?

You may need to gather requirements related to cryptographic authenticators into their own section or make sure they are grouped appropriately.

https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/authenticators/#sfc
https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/authenticators/#mfc
https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/syncable/#appB

New issue?

@elarlang, what do you think about the following long but hopefully clear proposal:

"_Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of sing"le-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, a hardware-based authentication mechanism is required that is tied to a particular device, provides impersonation resistance against phishing attacks (such as WebAuthn), and verifies intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key). A single factor mechanism that meets all these conditions is acceptable for L2 or L3.  Relaxing any of considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls._"

The requirement structure addresses the point and the reason why I opened the issue. The details for each part and level I leave for others to discuss.

And the requirement is going to replace the current 6.3.3 and 6.3.8, and will be moved to the first requirement in V6.5

I may be missing something, but doesn't Level 3 contain all the requirements from Level 2?
I would not merge them as it makes it really hard to read it.  It's better if 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 complement each other. I would rather say that for Level 2, 6.3.3 should be just fine, but for Level 3 you should consider both as required. 

If you need to make it very clear, do it like this:

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
|6.3.3 | Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. Relaxing this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls. | 2 & 3 | v5.0.be-2.2.9|

for Level 3: using a hardware-based authentication mechanism should mean using "either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms". There is no conflict between the two.

I just wanted to clarify again the problem this issue is trying to solve.

We now have a draconian and very prescriptive L3 requirement 6.3.8 that requires doing authentication in a certain way. This mechanisms for authentication basically obsoletes requirement 6.3.3 which provides various authentication options which would no longer be acceptable under L3.

The convention in ASVS is that requirements should always be additive, i.e. requirements for lower levels will also be relevant at the higher levels as well. Where we have seen a situation where a higher level requirement renders a lower level requirement irrelevant, we have merged these together. This is what we are doing here. I appreciate this may not have been immediately obvious but this is the rationale.

> I just wanted to clarify again the problem this issue is trying to solve.
> 
> We now have a draconian and very prescriptive L3 requirement 6.3.8 that requires doing authentication in a certain way. This mechanisms for authentication basically obsoletes requirement 6.3.3 which provides various authentication options which would no longer be acceptable under L3.
> 

I beg to differ; hardware-based authentication and mfa live as separate controls. You can perfectly well implement hardware-based authentication without MFA, but for AAL3, IAL3, FAL3, and eIDAS LoA3, you need to implement both MFA and hardware-based authentication. They are additive, not supplementary.

The problem to solve for the requirement is: "For authentication, MFA must be used". The rest are details based on levels (L2, L3) and up to the requirement wording.

What I don't like here is that we have a solution for one problem split into different requirements, or they can be in conflict under certain conditions.

> for AAL3, IAL3, FAL3, and eIDAS LoA3, you need to implement both MFA and hardware-based authentication. They are additive, not supplementary.

So I still think we don't want to bend over backwards to try and accommodate all the subtleties of these but I would modify something I wrote in the requirement as follows:

"_Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, one of the factors must be a hardware-based authentication mechanism that is tied to a particular device, provides impersonation resistance against phishing attacks (such as WebAuthn), and verifies intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key). Relaxing any of the considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls._"

That is fine given that you have the following under 6.3:

This section contains general requirements for the security of authentication mechanisms as well as setting out the different expectations for levels. In particular, enforcing the use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for L2, and hardware-based authentication, performed in an attested and trusted execution environment (TEE), is required for L3.

The phrase: _(such as WebAuthn)_ is not needed and is more confusing than helpful. It's a web standard. The key here is how you use it. 

You said: tied to a particular device. That is rather loose and can mean many things.

You should use the phrase: device bound  (see: https://www.passkeycentral.org/introduction-to-passkeys/passkey-types)

@tghosth I think you are missing several important aspects in your text: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3096#issuecomment-2857133019


I would not merge the text. Especially not if it is going to be the only requirement related to cryptographic authentication.

I would go for the text I suggested in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/3093/files

It seems more to the point and elegant than trying to merge what initially are multiple requirements into 1.

There are good reasons for including eIDAS LoA3 given that 400 million people are going to start using eIDAS LoA3 authenticators on a daily basis next year.

Would it make sense if I give you some background and logic with a call, how we build ASVS requirements?

Note that it is possible to edit your last comments instead of adding new ones, if there have not been anyone else's comments after your last comment :)

@elarlang, with all due respect. I appreciate the comment, but we disagree on this. The general MFA and hardware-based requirements should stay separate as they do today.

MFA and hardware-based authentication are additive, not supplementary requirements. The one does not replace the other. So you need them to be separate, not merged together.

> but we disagree on this

Disagree on what? I did not state anything here, just provided an opportunity to explain the background information on the logic for ASVS. If you don't care what is the logic behind and pushing changes in the other direction, it just causes a development deadlock. We have many issues on the topic with a lot of comments, but not much moving forward. The expected release date is at the end of the month.

For the reasons I just stated, I disagree with trying to merge 6.3.3 and 6.3.8. The fastest approach for resolving this would be to let them stay separate as they are today. I appreciate that you want to explain the background information on the logic for ASVS, but I don't see how that will help in this matter specifically.

To move as fast as possible I would suggest the following:

Both  6.3.3 and 6.3.8 fit perfectly well under 6.3 as "General Authentication Security". There is no reason to move it; it would just complicate things because you would need a separate section for cryptographic authentication. This issue highlights this specifically: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3096

If you want to move fast, then only, and I mean only, merge the changes I suggested. Do not move or create a new section, because that will make things more complicated and cause you to miss your deadline.

Later, in ASVS 5.1, you can add a separate section for cryptographic authentication and move what you view as more specific MFA and hardware-based requirement text into their own section, respectively. Does this make sense?

2nd line in the issue description:
> We have 2 MFA-related requirements in section "V6.3 General Authentication Security" but we also have a dedicated MFA-related section "V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements"

your comments

> Both 6.3.3 and 6.3.8 fit perfectly well under 6.3 as "General Authentication Security". There is no reason to move it; ...

> ... Do not move or create a new section, because that will make things more complicated and cause you to miss your deadline.

There is no section to create, we have a dedicated section for "V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements". I'm a bit confused by those statements. And surely in disagreement.
The reason I am saying what I am saying is that you must not, move hardware-based requirements under 6.5. They do not belong there.

> The reason I am saying what I am saying is that you must not, move hardware-based requirements under 6.5. They do not belong there.

Ack, got this point.

... but, based on the latest proposal (https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3094#issuecomment-2855126901) the requirement is about asking multi-factor authentication, where hardware-based component must be included as one factor. The requirement itself is not about hardware-based factors specifically.

Not today, but if you leave it as it is, you don’t need to break backward compatibility latter. The risk is that you need to move requirements back and forth. I agree that it’s a bit strange to have MFA under 6.3 when you have 6.5 as well, but, you can always clean it up in ASVS 5.1 if you are in a hurry and want to be ready for Global AppSec in Barcelona. Btw. See you there!

> hardware-based component must be included as one factor

There is much more to it then that. I have good reasons for saying what I am saying. Please, you will need a lot of time to go properly into this topic.

Ok so the move to 6.5 is contested and the merge is contested. If we were to keep it in 6.3, maybe we just compromise on the merge and the updated wording as follows:

## V6.3 General Authentication Security

This section contains general requirements for the security of authentication mechanisms as well as setting out the different expectations for levels.  L2 applications must force the use of multi-factor authentication (MFA). L3 applications must use hardware-based authentication, performed in an attested and trusted execution environment (TEE). This could include as device-bound passkeys, eIDAS LoA3 enforced authenticators, authenticators with AAL3 assurance, or an equivalent mechanism.

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **6.3.3** | Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, one of the factors must be a hardware-based authentication mechanism which provides compromise and impersonation resistance against phishing attacks while verifying the intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key or a mobile phone). Relaxing any of the considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls. | 2 | v5.0.be-2.2.9 |
This could work. You may end up splitting it again, but it leaves you with the option of moving and splitting it later if required.
@elarlang to open a PR based on the merge

As I said in the issue, the move is nice to have. What I don't like here, is the "reasoning" that ignores the explained rationale. So I think the move we did not make at the moment was not on the correct basis.

The move was first agreed in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3094#issuecomment-2853668693 and arguments to oppose the move are a bit out of context, the reasoning is in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/3094#issuecomment-2857840705.

Would it perhaps be an idea to merge this, than wait and see until everything nears completion?

Not my place to have an opinion, but you said you where in a hurry.

I believe that is what happened.

> Would it perhaps be an idea to merge this, than wait and see until everything nears completion?
> 
> Not my place to have an opinion, but you said you where in a hurry.

I believe that is what happened.

@elarlang do you want to keep this open for future discussion on moving or should we close for now?

title: Discussion: merge L2 and L3 MFA requirements (6.3.3, 6.3.8) and move to section V6.5
